bug_semantics: When CFG_WIDEVINE_PTA is enabled, core/pta/widevine.c:open_session() gates callers by UUID but unconditionally dereferences the calling session: ts_get_calling_session() is stored and is_user_ta_ctx(session->ctx) is invoked with no NULL test. A Normal World client that issues OPTEE_MSG_CMD_OPEN_SESSION directly on the Widevine pseudo-TA has no calling TA on the thread session stack, so ts_get_calling_session() returns NULL; the session->ctx load faults at S-EL1 and panics the TEE (CWE-476 DoS). Sibling PTAs already reject a NULL caller. The one-line fix is `if (!session || !is_user_ta_ctx(session->ctx))`.
flaw_origin: The NULL-unchecked caller gate was first written when the Widevine PTA itself was added. ad194957b67062673816128f89eededb83f4be5b created core/pta/widevine.c from /dev/null, including open_session() at lines 112-130 with `struct ts_session *session = ts_get_calling_session();` then `if (!is_user_ta_ctx(session->ctx))`. At that same tree, gprof/system/attestation PTAs already did `if (!s) return TEE_ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` before is_user_ta_ctx. The vulnerable lines were unchanged until the 2026 fix; this is a missing NULL check on a new PTA surface, not a later regression.
